title: PROGRESS UNDER PM-JANMAN
body_text:
The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed today  in Lok Sabha that the Government has made significant progress in providing basic facilities such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) in PVTG habitations. The details of the benefits given under PM JANMAN, as on 30.06.2026, Ministry-wise & State-wise and District-wise including in Maharashtra are given at Annexure I.
A total of 831 MMUs have been operationalised through Ministry of Health and Family Welfare as on 30.06.2026 under PM JANMAN to provide last-mile access to healthcare services. Under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), through Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, as of July 2026, 474 MMUs have been operationalized. Further under DAJGUA, Ministry of Tribal Affairs has approved 15 Centres of Competence (CoCs), a dedicated intervention for Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) treatment.
The Ministry has been urging the State Governments and line Ministries the need to achieve saturation of interventions (for eligible beneficiaries ) under the Abhiyan. The actual number beneficiaries to be covered under the abhiyan is subjected to eligibility criteria of specific guidelines of concerned interventions as per norms approved.
The Ministry is regularly coordinating with concerned line Ministries/Departments / State Tribal Welfare Department / other line State Departments for implementation of the existing interventions under the PM JANMAN to expedite the progress and achievements.
Based on the data captured through the habitation level mobile survey carried out by the State Government, 17 Districts of Maharashtra are having PVTG population. However, Akola District does not have PVTG population as per the survey.
No specific plan is under consideration in Ministry of Tribal Affairs. However, Ministry regularly reviews progress of projects and consultations are held with line Ministries and State Departments including Forest Departments for expedition resolution of relevant issues.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Lok Sabha on progress under PM-JANMAN, a mission for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), as of 30 June 2026. As of that date, 831 Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) had been operationalised under PM-JANMAN and 474 under DAJGUA, with 15 Centres of Competence approved for Sickle Cell Disease treatment. Detailed state- and district-wise data on housing, roads, water, health, education, electrification and connectivity were also tabled, including for Maharashtra where 17 districts have PVTG population (Akola does not).
enrichment.context: PM-JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan), launched in November 2023, is a Rs 24,000 crore mission aimed at saturating basic infrastructure and livelihood support—safe housing, clean drinking water, roads, electricity, telecom connectivity, health and education access—for the 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) across India, who are among the most marginalised communities due to their small population size, pre-agricultural technology, and geographic isolation. It converges resources from multiple ministries including Rural Development (PMAY-G, PMGSY), Health and Family Welfare, Jal Shakti (Jal Jeevan Mission), Women and Child Development (POSHAN 2.0), Education, Power, New and Renewable Energy, and Telecom. DAJGUA (Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan) is a related, broader village-development convergence scheme targeting all tribal-majority villages, not just PVTG habitations. Sickle Cell Disease has been a major focus area since the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission was launched in 2023, given its high prevalence in tribal populations; the Centres of Competence represent specialised treatment infrastructure under this broader elimination effort. Such periodic Parliamentary disclosures track saturation targets and reveal implementation gaps across states, useful for assessing governance and welfare delivery to vulnerable groups.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) is specifically targeted at which of the following groups?
options: All Scheduled Tribes notified under the Constitution
prelims_questions.explanation: PM-JANMAN is a mission specifically designed to provide basic facilities and livelihood support to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), a sub-category of Scheduled Tribes identified as more vulnerable due to factors like pre-agricultural technology and low population.

prelims_questions.question: Under PM-JANMAN, Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) are operationalised through which Ministry?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, 831 MMUs under PM-JANMAN and 474 MMUs under DAJGUA have been operationalised through the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (NRHM).

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of PM-JANMAN in addressing the developmental deficits of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs). What are the key challenges in achieving saturation of interventions under such convergence-based schemes?

Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups face unique health, infrastructural and livelihood challenges compared to other Scheduled Tribes. Examine the rationale behind their separate categorisation and evaluate government efforts to bridge the development gap.
